audit.summary: Printed preservation functional fails on translated ellipses and row-slot scaling gives a zero row in the claimed invertible limit. Concrete coordinated repairs, local formula corrections, positive proof checks and withdrawn circularity allegation are retained. Final geometric uniqueness statements are not disproved.
limitations: P1 — Incompatible angular origins invalidate the preservation functional — Counterevidence: Changing scalar, phase or orientation does not annihilate a nonzero paired vector. Coherent paired rotations preserve finite rank, but the originally mixed full operator is not already conjugate.

P2 — Row-slot index is incorrectly used in finite operator scaling — Counterevidence: No relabeling creates missing denominator3; finite prefactors do not correct exponent. Algebraic finite matrices remain nondegenerate after proper scaling.

P2 — Row-slot index is incorrectly used in finite operator scaling — Counterevidence: This remains a defect when the abstract Fourier coefficients are treated separately from P1. Source(6.11) attaches selected caustics to slots, while(4.1)/(4.33) use actual denominators; a relabeling or finite nonzero prefactor cannot manufacture denominator3. The algebraic nondegenerate finite matrices themselves are not refuted.

P3 — Exact sine and cosine coefficient families differ — Counterevidence: Mixed-parity vanishing is valid but does not equate unmixed entries; opposite-frequency term starts at least two orders above leading.

P4 — Uniform asymptotic bound requires a rotation ceiling — Counterevidence: If some constant means pair-dependent, no contradiction for fixed pair; that reading supplies no absolute uniform bound. Actual p1 tail has a fixed ceiling.

P5 — Printed lower spectral-separation bound contradicts strict chord length — Counterevidence: Numerical examples illustrate but strict geometric inequality proves contradiction. Corrected bound also excludes intermediate multiples for p>=3.

P6 — Reciprocal normalization in spectral-coefficient identification — Counterevidence: Potential Major circularity allegation withdrawn: author says follow ideas and distinguishes coefficients. Endpoint visibility before equality and positive separation polynomial provide explicit repair.

P6 — Reciprocal normalization in spectral-coefficient identification — Counterevidence: The source explicitly says to follow the ideas of preceding lemmas and distinguishes the coefficients. That permits the own-coefficient reconstruction; it does not justify retaining a categorical Major circularity allegation. Requiring visible endpoints for all large q is essential; an unspecified subsequence would not suffice.
Limitations: External KAM, normal-form, microlocal and full Heath-Brown proofs not independently rederived.
Limitations: The coherent repairs are bounded reviewer arguments, not a complete corrected edition or author adoption.
Limitations: Numerical checks are high-precision diagnostics, not interval certificates.

proposition.claim:
Elliptic tangent weights annihilate printed caustic-preservation functionals and caustic-preserving graphs obey a quadratic bound.

Fixed sufficiently small positive e, a1, x-translation t->0, p1q3; all caustics remain, bounded C5/C39 norms and stated smallness threshold.

Scaled operator tends to a block matrix with invertible finite Ahat.

Allowed q0=3; selected positive rational rotations strictly below1/3; finite row n6 and all column frequencies3..q1.

The two unmixed Fourier coefficient families agree exactly.

p1,qj3; elliptic nome expansion with paired Fourier symmetries.

One absolute constant controls advertised p/q<1/2 coefficient bound.

Interpretation as uniform absolute C; coprime j3,q2y+3,p(q-1)/2; take e->0 for each fixed pair then y->infinity.

t_pq >= (2p-1)ell/p for all relevant large periods.

Smooth strictly convex ellipse; p1 and arbitrarily large rational q.

Printed reciprocal map sends ellipse tail to integers and yields stated ratio.

c0,c>0, common perimeter and near-ellipse smallness; endpoints visible on every sufficiently large q.

repair.content:
Use quarter-period-corrected F, physical cos-squared motion weights and corresponding Jcorr, both Fourier sectors; exact first variation restores tangent annihilation. Quantitative uniform q8 theorem must be carried through consistently.

Replace left power by e^(q1-Q_n), preserving actual caustic constants and right power. Check bounded left factors, vanishing C, unchanged B, square-summable D-I. Normalize constant motion row separately.

Retain both branches; use common leading asymptotics only. Generating function gives general binomial coefficients.

Require p/q<=omega_max<1/2 with C and small-e threshold depending on ceiling.

Use (p-1/2)ell<t<=T<pell for bounded numerators after increasing q0 via existing asymptotics.

Use each domain's own coefficient to isolate visible intervals first; |n(q)-lambda q|<=Cepsilon+C'/q, every large-q integer gap1, then lambda1.
